original_question: Let M be a complex manifold of dimension n that is homogeneous under the action of a Lie group G, let 𝓜 be the space of holomorphic maps from M to Pn with the compact-open topology, and let G act on 𝓜 by precomposition. Under what conditions does this action admit a dense orbit?
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 9.3(i) of Some Open Problems on Holomorphic Foliation Theory.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies a complex manifold M homogeneous under a Lie group G, the space of holomorphic maps from M to P^n, the compact-open/topology of uniform convergence on compact sets, the induced action of G on that map space by precomposition, and the question of whether the action has a dense orbit. This is essentially the official formulation of Section 9, Problem 9.3(i).
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation sits in Section 9 ('Dynamics on the space of maps') and is motivated by the preceding discussion of Birkhoff-type dense orbits for spaces of holomorphic maps; that context should be reflected so the question is read as a hypercyclicity/universality problem, not as a general orbit-closure question.
To make the statement fully stand-alone, one should say that G acts transitively on M by holomorphic automorphisms; otherwise the induced action on holomorphic maps is not completely specified.
The target should be identified explicitly as complex projective space P^n(C), not an unspecified projective space over some other field.
The topology should be stated exactly as the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets (equivalently, the compact-open topology).
The induced action should be written explicitly, e.g. for a left action of G on M, (g·f)(x)=f(g^{-1}·x); saying only 'by precomposition' leaves the convention implicit.
Dense orbit should be unpacked as an existence statement: there exists f in Hol(M,P^n(C)) whose G-orbit is dense in Hol(M,P^n(C)).

No degree restriction, nilpotency hypothesis, ambient ring beyond C, or asymptotic clause such as 'for all sufficiently large m' is part of this problem; the refined statement should make clear that none of these extra conditions belong to the paper’s formulation.
refined_question: Let M be a complex manifold of complex dimension n, homogeneous under a Lie group G acting transitively by holomorphic automorphisms, and let Hol(M,P^n(C)) denote the space of holomorphic maps M -> P^n(C), endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. Consider the induced G-action on Hol(M,P^n(C)) by precomposition, for example (g·f)(x)=f(g^{-1}·x). Under what conditions on the homogeneous pair (M,G) does this action admit a dense orbit; equivalently, when does there exist f in Hol(M,P^n(C)) whose G-orbit is dense in Hol(M,P^n(C))?
justification: The draft is targeting the right place in the paper: Section 9 first recalls Birkhoff’s dense-translation-orbit phenomenon for entire maps and then explicitly proposes analogous questions for other source manifolds and automorphism groups. Immediately after that setup, Problem 9.3(i) asks, in essentially the same words, for conditions under which the induced action on holomorphic maps from a homogeneous complex manifold M to P^n admits a dense orbit. The rewrite therefore keeps the scope exactly at Problem 9.3(i) and only makes the hidden assumptions explicit: the holomorphic/transitive nature of the G-action on M, the target P^n(C), the topology, and the meaning of 'dense orbit.'
